QF.id: Taxation of Debt and Equity Products_15

question.text: An investment adviser is comparing post-tax returns for a client in the 30% tax bracket. The client has Rs.10,00,000 to invest for 18 months. Option A: Listed zero-coupon corporate bond whose entire 9% p.a. return arises as capital appreciation on sale, with the bond held for more than 12 months. Option B: Bank FD at 8% p.a. Option C: Debt mutual fund (80% debt, bought in 2025). Assuming all returns are realized, which option provides the highest post-tax return?

answer.text: Listed zero-coupon corporate bond — LTCG at 12.5% on capital appreciation is most tax-efficient
Bank FD — because FD interest is exempt up to Rs.50,000 under Section 80TTB
Debt mutual fund — because it qualifies for LTCG at 12.5% after 12 months
All three have the same post-tax return since all debt income is taxed at slab rate

explanation.text: The Logic: Listed zero-coupon bond held >12 months: the entire return is capital appreciation, taxed as LTCG at 12.5% (not slab rate). This is the most tax-efficient. Bank FD at 8%: interest is taxed at slab rate (30%), so post-tax return = 8% x (1 - 0.30) = 5.6% p.a. Section 80TTB is for senior citizens only, not applicable here. Debt MF (80% debt, bought in 2025): this is a Specified Mutual Fund Type 1 under Section 50AA (>=65% debt/money market instruments), so gains are ALWAYS short-term at slab rate = 30% effective tax. Listed zero-coupon bond: 9% appreciation, with LTCG at 12.5%, post-tax return ~ 9% x (1 - 0.125) = 7.875% p.a. — the highest. The Trap: Option B tempts candidates who confuse Section 80TTA (savings account interest) with Section 80TTB (senior citizen FD interest). Option C is the biggest trap — many assume debt MFs still get LTCG, but Specified MFs (>=65% debt) are always short-term at slab rate under Section 50AA. Option D wrongly assumes uniform taxation. Note: NISM Series X-B workbook (pages 206-208, 215-217) supports that interest on bonds is taxable as interest income at applicable rates while only the capital gain on listed bonds held more than 12 months is taxed at 12.5% LTCG. The stem here therefore restricts Option A to a zero-coupon listed bond whose entire return is capital appreciation. Specified Mutual Fund Type 1 treatment under Section 50AA is also drawn from the workbook.
